questions.question: Which of the following sequences correctly orders the early milestones in reinforcement learning (RL) as mentioned in the context?

options.A: Turing (1954) → Samuel (1959) → Minsky’s SNARC (1954) → Waltz & Fu (1965)
options.B: Minsky’s SNARC (1954) → Turing (1954) → Samuel (1959) → Waltz & Fu (1965)
options.C: Turing (1954) → Minsky’s SNARC (1954) → Samuel (1959) → Waltz & Fu (1965)
options.D: Samuel (1959) → Turing (1954) → Waltz & Fu (1965) → Minsky’s SNARC (1954)

questions.explanation:
The context lists the idea of programming a computer to learn by trial and error (Turing, 1954), followed by SNARC (Minsky, 1954), Samuel’s checkers program (1959), and later work in the 1960s such as Waltz & Fu (1965) [Page 82].

questions.question: According to the passage, which view of AI was heavily criticized during the AI winter, prompting a shift toward learning and probabilistic modeling?

options.A: The belief‑aggregation approach that combines past observations into a belief state.
options.B: The view that “logic doesn’t work,” implying that AI itself does not work.
options.C: The perspective that deep learning alone constitutes true AI.
options.D: The stance that reinforcement learning is the only viable AI paradigm.

questions.explanation:
The text notes that in the AI winter many researchers claimed “logic doesn’t work,” leading to the conclusion that AI doesn’t work and suggesting a focus on learning and probabilistic modeling [Page 199].

---

questions.question: What term does the context use to refer to the classical AI approach that builds deterministic knowledge bases from data?
questions.explanation:
The passage states that first‑order logic (FOL) is exactly what is sometimes called “Good Old‑Fashioned AI” (GOFAI) [Page 199].

questions.question: Which development around 2011 is identified in the context as sparking a new wave of optimism known as the “spring of AI”?

options.A: The rise of deep learning in media coverage.
options.D: Introduction of stochastic neural‑analog reinforcement calculators.

questions.explanation:
The text mentions that around 2011, modern research on relational machine learning led to new optimism dubbed the “spring of AI” [Page 199].

questions.question: Which statement best captures the shift in policy representation described in the context, moving away from belief‑based aggregation?

options.A: Policies now incorporate belief states to better handle uncertainty.
options.B: Policies directly map a fixed‑size history window to actions, discarding belief aggregation.
options.C: Policies are replaced entirely by deterministic rule‑based systems.
options.D: Policies rely on exhaustive enumeration of all possible world states.

questions.explanation: The passage advises to “discard the idea of using belief to ‘aggregate’ history” and instead map history directly to actions via policies [Page 110].
